name: VAG DQ381 / 0GC 7-speed DSG TCU

read_methods.notes: Per OpenTune's bosch-dq381 definition: a complete original needs a bench/boot read (the 0x188000-byte full read the checksum was validated on); calibration flashing may be possible over OBD (UDS on CAN).

notes: Seven-speed wet-clutch DSG (refined DQ380, 2017+) used across MQB models (Wikipedia names the Arteon). OpenTune's dq381 checksum (BOOT/ASW/CAL CRC-32) is validated on a real full dump. The pinout below comes from one source whose connector description is internally inconsistent (it calls the plug 10-pin but numbers pins up to 16), so the unit-level confidence is 'unverified' - check every pin.

connectors.name: TCU
connectors.description: Gearbox (mechatronic) connector as drawn by ecupinouts ('VAG DQ500' connector)

bench.notes: ecupinouts: +12 V to 9 and 15, ground 16, CAN-H 6 / CAN-L 7. Single source with an inconsistent connector description - verify on the unit.
bench.resistor_notes: Put a 120 ohm resistor across CAN-H/CAN-L if your interface does not terminate.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.
